subject: share an R object between shinyApps

messages.author: 7fc8ada95bdc26b2
messages.subject: share an R object between shinyApps
parts:
Hi,

please does anyone know if there is a way to use the same R object (e.g. a data table) created in a shinyApp (e.g. shinyApp1) in a second shinyApp opened right after (e.g. shinyApp2)?
Here the example, I have 2 shinyapps in the same server location

# Define the location '/'
location / {
  site_dir /srv/shiny-server/

}+---/srv/shiny-server
|   +---shinyApp1
|       +---server.R
|       +---ui.R
|   +---shinyApp2
|       +---server.R
|       +---ui.R

so that the user is using shinyApp1, and it works on a datatable (that becames an R object data() ).
Then, the user opens shinyApp2 as link to the new application

with the ui.R tag in shinyApp1 

tags$a(href="/shinyApp2", target="_blank", "text of link"),

so I would like that user is able to work on the R object data().

Thank you!!!

messages.author: 2a8dcf5b378ecca9
messages.subject: Re: share an R object between shinyApps
parts:
Somewhat related, but I used a common google sheet that one app could append rows to and the other was so that the administrator could watch multiple respondents fill a data sheet.  The administrator could also edit.  The users also had a tab that allowed them to review their previous answers, so the data went round and round.  It was plenty fast and worked well.  

The other way I have done it is to allow the app user to edit a hanson table and then when they click on a "submit changes" button the table is written to disk or remote data storage.  After writing the data to storage it was read back in and assigned to the global environment so that other "tabs" could use the updated information.

You can also embed a google sheet, check out jennybc on github for the google sheets package and the shinysky package for the hanson tables.

I think Dean Attalia (sorry if I mangled the name) is on here frequently and his blog post about mimicking a google form might give you some ideas as well.
